title: Per-tenant and per-model circuit breaker with graceful fallback routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a hierarchical circuit-breaker framework that can be configured per-dependency, per-model, and per-tenant. The system should detect short-term and sustained failures (errors and latency regressions) and automatically route requests to safe fallbacks while preserving correctness and privacy. Scope: runtime messaging layer + router + Console config + metrics/alerts. Not in scope: model-level retraining or business logic changes to downstream clients. Key requirements: (1) allow independent thresholds (error %, p95 latency) for dependency/model/tenant; (2) support both open and closed windows (exponential backoff for recovery attempts); (3) deterministic fallback routing: downgraded model variant, cached response, or synthetic stub; (4) safe modes for private deployments where fallbacks must not leak tenant data; (5) multi-region coordination to avoid cascading trips during regional failovers. Deliverables: runtime config schema, router implementation, Console UI toggle and rollout plan, e2e test harness and chaos tests, alert rules and dashboards. Acceptance criteria: reproducible trips in staging, automated fallback trigger within configured SLO budget, no customer data leakage in private deploys, and clear observability (per-tenant metrics + per-model circuit state).
comments: 2026-02-21: Initial design doc posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Reliability/Per-tenant+Circuit+Breaker+Proposal — includes example thresholds and state machine diagrams.

2026-02-23: Sync notes — decided to support two trip signals: error-rate (5xx/failure %) and latency (p95 > threshold). Miguel prefers sliding-window counters for low-latency detection; Aisha requested an option for exponential moving average for noisy tenants.

2026-02-26: Engineering review comments — need to ensure atomic update of circuit state across replicas. Proposal: use leader-elected shard for per-tenant state or rely on strongly-consistent store (etcd) for private deployments. Trade-off noted: higher round-trip vs potential stale state in eventual stores.
2026-03-02: Implementation started — added feature flags to enable per-tenant override; basic metrics emitted: circuit_state, trips_count, last_trip_reason.

2026-03-05: Design review feedback from PM (Ravi): require explicit fallback policy per-tenant to meet contractual SLAs. Added policy schema: ["fallback_to": "model-variant", "fallback_cache_ttl": 600, "deny_fallback_for_tenant": false]

2026-03-09: Observability update — created dashboard and SLO burn rate alerts: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/CB-dashboard/per-tenant-cb. Noted flapping in staging when thresholds were too aggressive; increased hysteresis and minimum evaluation window to 60s.

2026-03-11: Security review (brief) — private deploys must not return cached responses that include cross-tenant content. Implemented cache keying by tenant and added a flag 'require_tenant_isolation' in config.

2026-03-12: QA report — succeeded in simulated regional failover: circuits in failed region tripped and directed traffic to remote region with degraded-model fallback. Latency increase measured and within SLO burn budget.
test_plan: Unit tests for state machine transitions, integration tests that simulate error spike/latency spike, chaos tests (kill model worker, delay kernel) in staging, regression check that fallback preserves response schema and content safety. Load test to validate trip thresholds under bursty traffic patterns. Manual validation for private deploy to ensure tenant isolation during fallback.
rollback_plan: Feature-flag gating: disable per-tenant breakers and route all traffic to primary models. Emergency kill-switch in Console that sets 'allow_fallback=false' and resets circuit states. Keep a step-by-step runbook linked in attachments.
monitoring: Expose metrics: cb_state{tenant,model,region}, cb_trips_total, cb_recoveries_total, cb_fallback_count. Alerts: (1) more than 5% of active tenants tripped in 5m (alert SEV2), (2) a single tenant trips > 3 times in 1h (alert ops), (3) fallback invocation rate > configured SLA allowance (burn-rate alert). Dashboards per-tenant + heatmap by region and model.
implementation_notes: Implementation sketch: 1) add CB policy store (config proto) with layered precedence: global -> region -> tenant -> model. 2) runtime token bucket to track QPS and sliding windows for errors/latency. 3) router: if CB is 'open' choose fallback per policy (variant, cache, stub) and return with metadata headers (x-cb-state, x-fallback-reason). 4) recovery: probe small sample of traffic (1%) with circuit half-open and require N consecutive successes before closing. Trade-offs: per-tenant leader introduces complexity for multi-region failover; chosen approach uses per-region state with eventual reconciliation plus a strong-store option for private installs.
notes: Avoiding data leakage is highest priority for private customers. Any cached fallback must be tenant-scoped. Fallbacks that may synthesize or redact content require PM signoff.
